_comment: Hologram models (VECTOR's format: vector's tools/holo/collection.py and assets/holo/README.md). Boxes are [x0,x1, y0,y1, z0,z1] in fractions of the normalised bounding box (y up, front +z); a face goes to the first part whose box holds its centroid, else to the part with rest=true. bind names the live reading a part shows (VECTOR's holo/bind.py), empty for a part that only shapes the model. Sources are in src/; the baked NAME.holo.npz sit next to this file. Rebake: ~/.local/share/bromigos/venv/bin/python <vector>/tools/holo/bake.py --root THIS_DIR --preview

parts.label: HEAD AND BARBELS
parts.hint: The blunt head and its fringe of barbels. The Choir's songs travel on the old analog bands; every trawler radio on Tidewell hears them as long tones under the static

parts.label: TAIL FAN
parts.hint: The fan tail: sailors swear they sometimes hear a phrase on the radio seconds before it comes up through the hull

parts.label: FINS
parts.hint: Wide veined fins: seen from the surface, the Choir is only slow light moving under the swell

parts.label: FINS
parts.hint: Nobody hunts the Choir. Ask a trawler crew why and every crew gives the same answer: they're listening

parts.label: LIGHT ORGANS
parts.hint: The row of light organs along the flank, in the Choir's cyan. Maren Holt logs every song: time, bearing, depth and the shape of every phrase

parts.label: BELL BUOY
parts.hint: The bell buoy riding off the rock's lee: the black flame is painted on it, riding the swell

parts.label: LAMP ROOM
parts.hint: The lamp room: the colony's weather and distress beacon went dark in the Switch-Off and came back with a relay in it. Lit while every channel on the network answers

parts.label: KEEPER'S COTTAGE
parts.hint: Where Maren logs the Choir's songs: time, bearing, depth and the shape of every phrase. The best record of the Echo anyone in the network keeps

parts.label: TOWER
parts.hint: The tower: small, older than the platforms, and nobody agrees who built it

parts.label: THE SLIVER
parts.hint: A knife of black rock a few hundred metres from the oldest platform: the only land on Tidewell anyone has charted. Below it the kelp shelves fall into the deep, where the Choir sings
